project.name: lpc-toolkit
project.description: A monorepo providing a shared, environment-agnostic core for composing LPC character sprites, a React web UI, and a planned CLI. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the repository README to understand why lpc-toolkit exists: it turns migrated Liberated Pixel Cup assets into composable character sprites through a shared core and a React editor. It also introduces the pnpm monorepo layout, the GPL and attribution obligations, and the planned CLI that will reuse the same environment-agnostic library.

tour.title: Workspace Structure
tour.description: The root manifest defines the commands that coordinate packages, while the workspace file establishes which packages participate in those commands. Read these after the overview to see how core and web are developed together without collapsing their separate runtime responsibilities.
tour.languageLesson: A pnpm workspace links local packages through a shared dependency graph, so the web package can consume the core package while each package retains its own manifest and build settings.

tour.title: Browser Bootstrap
tour.description: The Vite entry point mounts the React application, and App becomes the shell that loads local catalog and palette data before initializing the editor. Together they show the browser startup boundary and the first handoff from framework setup to application state.
tour.languageLesson: React StrictMode intentionally exercises components more aggressively in development, which helps reveal unsafe effects and lifecycle assumptions before production.

tour.title: Editor Orchestration
tour.description: Building on App's loaded data, the layer-stack harness coordinates the main editing workspace and the selection reducer defines how chosen sprite layers change. This is the best overview of the interactive flow because it connects user controls, reducer state, previews, and export actions without hiding the state transitions.
tour.languageLesson: Reducer-driven state makes complex UI transitions explicit: each action describes an event, and the reducer computes the next immutable selection state.

tour.title: Core Public API
tour.description: The core index is the most depended-on file in the graph and defines the package surface that both the web UI and future CLI are expected to consume. API.md explains the contracts and design decisions behind those exports, turning the barrel file into a readable map of the environment-agnostic library.
tour.languageLesson: A TypeScript barrel module re-exports selected symbols from internal modules, presenting consumers with a stable public API while allowing implementation files to remain focused.

tour.title: Core Contracts
tour.description: The shared types establish the vocabulary for assets, selections, frames, and composition results, while adapters define the image-loading and canvas capabilities supplied by callers. The catalog module turns asset definitions into validated data that the rest of the pipeline can query, preserving the core package's independence from browser and Node globals.
tour.languageLesson: Dependency inversion keeps the core portable: interfaces describe required capabilities, and runtime-specific packages provide concrete implementations.

tour.title: Composition Pipeline
tour.description: With the contracts in place, frame selection determines which rectangles belong to an animation, recoloring transforms palette-driven pixels, and compose combines ordered layers into final frames. These modules are the central sprite-processing path and show how deterministic data operations are separated from runtime-specific image creation.

tour.title: Browser Integration
tour.description: The browser canvas adapter supplies the capabilities required by the core contracts, while the catalog loader binds Vite-managed local assets into the application. The composition hook then connects React state to asynchronous core composition, caching results and preventing stale work from replacing newer selections.
tour.languageLesson: React hooks can encapsulate asynchronous pipelines, but they must guard against stale completions when dependencies change before an earlier operation finishes.

tour.title: Attribution And Export
tour.description: Credits are resolved and formatted alongside composed output so attribution remains part of the product contract rather than an optional UI detail. The ZIP exporter carries that metadata into downloadable animation-grouped PNG bundles, demonstrating how the web layer preserves the core library's licensing guarantees.

tour.title: Asset Preparation
tour.description: The asset release configuration pins the migrated source release, prepare-assets materializes the browser-ready asset tree, and validate-assets checks that the resulting data satisfies core rules. This build-time boundary explains how legacy upstream material becomes local, validated input without making the read-only submodule part of application runtime.

tour.title: Quality And Delivery
tour.description: The web package manifest ties together Vite, Vitest, Playwright, and asset scripts, while the GitHub Actions workflow runs repository checks on pushes and pull requests. End the tour here to see how strict typing, tests, builds, and asset validation protect the architecture described in the preceding steps.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use event triggers, jobs, and ordered steps to turn repository commands into repeatable CI gates.
